world.title: AMECEA PLENARY: “Do not be Robbed of Hope,” Cardinal Czerny to Young People at 21st AMECEA Plenary
world.description:
Sr. Jecinter Antoinette Okoth, FSSA
At the opening Mass of the 21st Plenary Assembly of the Association of Member Episcopal Conferences in Eastern Africa (AMECEA) on Sunday, July, 19, His Eminence Cardinal Michael Czerny urged young people not to lose hope in the face of a turbulent world.
Anchoring his reflection in Jesus' parables of the wheat and the weeds, the mustard seed, and the yeast, Cardinal Czerny, the Prefect of the Dicastery of Promoting Integral Human Development (PIHD), said the Kingdom of heaven is not something distant or abstract but is already present among believers, requiring attention and active participation to grow.
He further reflected on Pope Leo XIV's first Encyclical Letter Magnifica Humanitas and noted that Christians are called to be servants of the coming Kingdom. Thus, he continued, the Pope's teaching does not stop at simply pointing out what is wrong in the world, but instead invites believers to see history through the lens of the risen Christ, understanding the present moment not as a fixed fate but as a genuine opportunity for both personal and collective conversion.
Addressing tens of thousands of young people who attended the opening Mass at the Catholic University in Eastern Africa (CUEA), the Vatican representative focused on the day’s reading on the parable of the mustard seed.
He said the image captures how goodness can quietly take root and expand even amid widespread confusion and hardship, much as a tiny seed eventually grows into something far greater. He noted that this is a call to a hope that resists negativity.
Warning against what Pope Leo has called a false realism, true Christian witness, the cardinal said, goes beyond denouncing evil, toward actively discerning and walking the new paths the Lord is already opening.
Do not let yourselves be robbed of hope, the Cardinal said, drawing from Pope Francis’ 2013 homily, encouraging the young people to hold onto the image of the seed and to ask God for the grace to build bridges of hope, living out the prayer and the work of Thy Kingdom come.
Turning to the parable of the wheat and the weeds, the cardinal highlighted the patience of the landowner who, rather than uprooting the weeds immediately, chooses to wait until harvest so as not to damage the wheat growing alongside them. He described this as a model of prudent, faith-filled restraint, one that recognizes the real opposition between good and evil without resorting to hasty or purely punitive responses that risk destroying good that is still quietly taking shape.
Cardinal Czerny linked this to Pope Leo's reflections on international relations in Magnifica Humanitas, where the Pope describes dialogue as an essential diplomatic tool for preventing conflict and restoring trust between nations. Even amid aggressive rhetoric and power politics, the Pope's encyclical calls for humility and patience in nurturing whatever signs of goodwill exist among parties in conflict, in order to advance the cause of peace.
world.source: Association of Member Episcopal Conferences in Eastern Africa

world.title: AMECEA PLENARY: AMECEA Chairman Makes Youth a Pastoral Priority
world.description:
By Luke Bisani
The Chairman of the Association of Member Episcopal Conferences in Eastern Africa (AMECEA), Rt. Rev. Charles Kasonde, has declared young people a pastoral priority for the Catholic Church in the region over the next four years.
Bishop Kasonde made the declaration during the Opening Mass of the 21st AMECEA Plenary being held in Kenya, where he said the Church considers young people as a vital force in sustaining the Catholic faith and advancing evangelization for generations to come.
“Your Bishops make young people our pastoral priority for the next four years for three reasons: We want to demonstrate that young people are worth the effort and to help them develop a sense of belonging to this Holy Mother Church,” said Bishop Kasonde.
He said the Church’s previous engagements with young people, including major gatherings in Kampala, Uganda, and Ethiopia, had demonstrated the important role of the youth in keeping the Church vibrant and strengthening its evangelisation mission.
Bishop Kasonde further pointed to the Church’s longstanding commitment to young people, recalling the 1989 AMECEA Plenary, which focused on youth under the theme, “Youth on the Move Towards the Year 2000.”
He also highlighted the commitment of the Holy Fathers to addressing the aspirations and challenges facing young people through their teachings and encyclicals. He cited Pope Leo XIV’s recent message to young people, which encouraged them to use the internet responsibly.
The AMECEA Chairman urged young delegates participating in the plenary to become ambassadors of hope for the millions of young people across Eastern Africa who were unable to attend the gathering.
He also commended the Catholic Church in Kenya for agreeing to host the 21st AMECEA Plenary at short notice.
The plenary is being held under the theme, “AMECEA’s Synodal Journey with Young People: Building Bridges of Communion, Hope, Justice and Good Governance.”
world.source: Association of Member Episcopal Conferences in Eastern Africa

science.title: IL-2(N88D)/CD25 Fusion Protein Enhances Expansion of Antigen-Specific CD8⁺ T Cells to Suppress Hepatocellular Carcinoma
science.description: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a major cause of cancer-related death worldwide, with limited efficacy of current immunotherapies due to an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment and dysfunctional CD8⁺ tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs). Among these, PD-1⁺CD25⁺ CD8⁺ T cells represent a tumor-reactive subset linked to IL-2 responsiveness and favorable responses to PD-1 blockade. In this study, we integrated single-cell and spatial transcriptomics with clinical immunotherapy cohort analyses to characterize the phenotype and function of PD-1⁺CD25⁺ CD8⁺ TILs in human HCC. To therapeutically exploit this subset, we engineered IL-2(N88D)/CD25 fusion proteins with trimeric receptor bias, selectively promoting the expansion of PD-1⁺CD25⁺ CD8⁺ T cells. These constructs were tested in multiple murine HCC models, including orthotopic and hydrodynamic tail vein injection systems. PD-1⁺CD25⁺ CD8⁺ TILs were enriched in HCC tumors, particularly in immunotherapy responders, and exhibited enhanced tumor reactivity and neoantigen specificity. Treatment with IL-2/CD25 led to increased CD8⁺ T cell infiltration and delayed tumor progression with minimal toxicity, while the IL-2(N88D)/CD25 variant further boosted infiltration, activation, and survival outcomes. These findings highlight the therapeutic potential of selectively activating antigen-specific CD8⁺ T cells via IL-2(N88D)/CD25 fusion proteins, offering a promising strategy for improving HCC immunotherapy. An IL-2(N88D)/CD25 fusion protein selectively expands antigen-specific CD8⁺ T cells, enhances antitumor immunity, and suppresses hepatocellular carcinoma while minimizing regulatory T cell expansion.

science.title: Rates of passerine body plan evolution in time and space
science.description: The rates and patterns of phenotypic evolution are known to vary dramatically across time and space, yet the drivers of this variation remain poorly understood. Using over 170,000 skeletal measurements across 2,057 species of Passeriformes—the most diverse order of living birds—we reconstruct the evolutionary history of passerine body plan diversification over the past ~50 Myr. We find that the history of passerine body plan evolution is dominated by rare, hierarchically nested bursts of phenotypic innovation near the origins of major taxonomic groups, indicating that such radiations have played a disproportionately large role in shaping global passerine diversity. These bursts are temporally aligned with intervals of increased climatic instability in Earth’s history and are reflected in contemporary latitudinal gradients, where assemblages at higher latitudes host species with elevated mean rates of phenotypic evolution and more modular trait covariation. Together, our findings support the hypothesis that climatic variability may act as a recurring driver of phenotypic diversification, linking deep-time pulses of innovation to broad-scale spatial patterns in evolutionary tempo. A reconstruction of the evolutionary history of passerine body plans over the past ~50 Myr shows rare bursts of phenotypic innovation near the origin of major taxonomic groups that are temporally aligned with periods of increased climatic instability. Similar patterns are reflected in contemporary spatial gradients, where higher-latitude and more seasonal environments show elevated phenotypic rates.
